purpose: Teach: 製剤/仏像/床屋/駅伝/あご/観音/水銀/スマイル

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが新薬製剤の研究をされたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, my father used to do research on new pharmaceuticals.
lines.style: Nostalgic, measured delivery. Soft opening. The voice of someone reaching back into memory, speaking with gentle certainty. Slight pause between thoughts, as if watching the memory play out.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お寺の仏像を拝みに通ってらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and Grandpa, you used to go pray at the temple to that Buddha statue, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm and knowing, with a thread of affection underneath. Gentle correction offered as a shared memory, not a challenge. Slight rise at the end like she's inviting him into the recollection with her.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが近所の床屋に通われたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, my father used to go to the local barbershop regularly.
lines.style: Same measured, wistful tone as before. Quiet persistence in the voice — a small, specific memory being held carefully. No rush to the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、駅伝の応援にお出かけになったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, you used to go out to cheer for the relay race, didn't you?
lines.style: Gentle persistence. A soft smile in the voice. She's offering another shared memory, tender but patient — as if she's used to this small dance between them.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがあごひげを蓄えられたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, my father grew a beard on his chin.
lines.style: The same wistful tone holds. A smaller detail this time, almost meditative. The voice settles into the image of it — not grand, just present.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、観音様にお参りされてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, you used to pay your respects at the Kannon shrine, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, playful affection now, barely concealed. A knowing tone — she's remembering something that brings her joy. The correction is gentle, almost teasing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが水銀の体温計を持ってらしたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, my father used to carry a mercury thermometer.
lines.style: Quieter now, more tender underneath the wistfulness. This is a small, intimate detail — the kind of thing you notice when you love someone. The voice lingers slightly.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、孫を見ると素敵なスマイルになられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, when you saw your grandchildren, you'd get such a lovely smile on your face, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, close, and tender. A smile in every word. She's moved from correcting to affirming something beautiful. Softer delivery, like she's speaking from the heart. Slight trailing warmth at the end.
